Rumors about next year’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models have been ramping up, and they suggest Apple is designing an ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ that combines traits from two current models.

Recent findings suggest that apple keeps expanding the iPhone line to include new models. And while it’s great that there are more models for differing preferences and needs, it’s also left me missing the days of having one model that was the clear “best.”.

That problem isn’t going away, since the iPhone Duo represents a brand new type of iPhone that some owners will love, while others find it isn’t for them.

With my failed iPhone Duo experiment over, I’m back to using iPhone 18 Pro as my default model. But I still have an iPhone Air around for work, and every time I pick it up, I’m struck by how impressive it remains.

Industry observers note that I used the iPhone Air all of last year and loved it. The main reason I upgraded to an iPhone 18 Pro is the camera system. I have young children at home—including newborn twins—and want to capture the best possible photos before they get older.

iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera has been fantastic, and it’s great having the Telephoto again too.

But I still sorely miss the overall design of the iPhone Air. And it sounds like next year, I could get the best of both models.

Rumors indicate Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models will have a unique new design featuring a quad-curved display that makes it look bezel-free.

The newly introduced models are expected to also be a bit slimmer, use curved edges, and possibly even bring back titanium. Leakers say the new design borrows a lot from the iPhone Air’s look.

This sounds like exactly what I’ve been hoping for.

According to recent reports, if they make one the size of the iPhone 13 mini I will buy. Otherwise I'm holding out.

While the ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ certainly won’t—and shouldn’t—be as thin as iPhone Air, if it can slim down a little and adopt several other Air design traits, I suspect it will evoke the same affection the Air has.

But unlike the Air, the upcoming Pro model will still offer the best camera system in an iPhone (not to mention better battery life).

Recent findings suggest that as a huge fan of the design of the Air, and the functionality of the 18 Pro, Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone model could prove the perfect model for me. And for anyone else not opting for iPhone Duo 2.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that gauthier, one of America’s best living songwriters, has had her songs recorded by everyone from Boy George to Blake Shelton, and earned a Grammy nomination in 2019 for her album Rifles & Rosary Beads, which featured collaborations with U.S.
  • Industry observers note that even so, it’s hard not to marvel at the compositions that make up Reckoning, an album that has quietly evolved into a soundtrack to the country’s political shift.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mary Gauthier has always had the innate ability to make her listeners confront some hard truths in her songs, often without them realizing they’ve done so until halfway through. She did it most memorably in 1999 with “I Drink,” a stark ballad about her battle with alcoholism that, despite its sing-song melody, was matter-of-fact in its depiction of addiction.

Industry observers note that gauthier, one of America’s best living songwriters, has had her songs recorded by everyone from Boy George to Blake Shelton, and earned a Grammy nomination in 2019 for her album Rifles & Rosary Beads, which featured collaborations with U.S. veterans. The songwriting process can seem especially magical to those not gifted with the skill, but Gauthier pulled back the curtain in her 2021 book Saved by a Song, showing exactly how she starts and continuously refines a song.

Industry observers note that even so, it’s hard not to marvel at the compositions that make up Reckoning, an album that has quietly evolved into a soundtrack to the country’s political shift. The title track all but predicted the seismic November midterms, in which an electorate fed up with government corruption, an unwanted war, and an untenable cost of living, gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress, plus a majority of governorships.

“You can cut down all the flowers, but you cannot stop the spring/There’s a pendulum in motion, and you can’t outrun the swing,” Gauthier presciently sings in “Reckoning,” which she co-wrote with the equally forward-looking Aaron Lee Tasjan. It’s an unconventional, Dylan-like composition, made up of six verses and not a single chorus. The closest it comes is when each verse’s payoff line circles back to the idea of a “reckoning.”.

According to recent reports, “Voices shoved into the shadows, will join and rise in time/A reckoning is breaking through, a hidden hand is moving by design,” goes the last lyric of the second verse. In the fourth, she identifies the reckoning in a blowing wind of change; in the fifth, she compares it to a river rolling in.

That reckoning, Gauthier assures us, was destined to arrive in due time: We’ve been through far too much to not have things set right. But in case you’ve missed all the injustice that’s gone down since the beginning of time, the 64-year-old sums it up in the eviscerating “Soldier of Fortune.” Trending Stories Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Snapshots From Miley’s Wedding: ‘Beautiful’ to See Family ‘United by Love’ Anthem Singer Apologizes for ‘O Canada’ Flub at Leafs-Islanders Game U2 Will Bring Their ‘Greatest Show on Earth’ Stadium Tour to North America in 2027 Watch Taylor Swift Surprise Brenda Lee With ‘Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree’ Honor.

Starting with the Romans’ crucifixion of Christ, she skewers the soulless brutes who’ve always done history’s dirty work. It ends with a devastating verse about the ICE killings of Renée Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. “You’re nothing but a gun for hire, hiding behind a mask,” Gauthier writes of the anonymous agents carrying out the administration’s un-American immigration policy.

In a recent development, but even those masked men can’t escape what Gauthier saw coming. In the final verse of the album’s title track, she offers one last comparison of the “reckoning” — a wave welcoming us home. It’s impossible to not see it as a blue one.

This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • Sources indicate that in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first confirmed. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

Sources indicate that in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

Recent findings suggest that the simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you said) to your “Notes to self” note.

To take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

According to recent reports, all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

Sources indicate that it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

In a recent development, there’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can proposal them better next time.

Recent findings suggest that you’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

Recent findings suggest that but this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

In a recent development, the Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I said it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

Roborock’s 2026 flagship model offers the ultimate in truly intelligent cleaning thanks to a combination of raw cleaning power and a market-leading combination of smart features.

Sources indicate that the benefits begin with a combination of raw power, reach, and fully automated self-cleaning. The Saros 20 delivers 36,000 Pa suction power with a dual anti-tangle system, ensuring no hassle with even the toughest of pet hairs, while a FlexiArm system ensures true edge-to-edge cleaning. The fully automated dock takes care of emptying the dust as well as washing and drying the mops.

AdaptiLift Chassis 3.0 enables the Saros 20 to move freely around the most largest and most complex of homes. A combination of an advanced vision system, adaptive algorithms, and a mechanical system comprising a main wheel, auxiliary wheel, and climbing arm mean that the device can cope with most thresholds between rooms. This even includes double layer thresholds, totaling 3.46 inches.

The Saros 20 uses StarSight Autonomous System 2.0, an industry-first navigation system with true 3D mapping of your home. The setup combines LiDAR with time-of-flight measurements to create an accurate depth map with both visual and infrared camera systems. The specs are unrivaled, with a sampling frequency more than 20 times higher than other devices and 21,600 sensor points, but what counts are the results. The AI powered system can recognize more than 300+ types of obstacles, even when they are are less than an inch in width and height. That means it can avoid anything from a loose cable to an inquisitive pet.

In a recent development, adaptiLift technology combines with a Carpet Intelligence System to enables the Saros 20 to detect when it is moving from solid flooring to carpet. At the most basic level, this means the mops will never get your carpets wet, but the system is far more sophisticated than this. The robot will automatically lift itself up onto deep pile carpets before lowering to the optimal height for vacuuming. It can cope with carpets with a pile height of 1.18 inches.

Sources indicate that finally, Smart Plan 3.0 is the AI-powered intelligent cleaning system that analyzes your home’s unique layout, floor materials, and the behavior patterns of everyone in the home in order to automatically optimise its cleaning routines. You also get voice and app control and can even check on your pets while away by asking the Saros 20 to locate them and provide a live video feed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Elev8on Management has spent years finding American talent routes on to European screens, and now its going help them build business empires there.

Sources indicate that the Paris-based talent management company has teamed with French wealth advisory Anato Gestion Privée to launch Elev8on Private, a division aimed at finding U.S. talent investment opportunities in Europe. We hear a prospectus has been readied with potential investment opportunities outlined.

In a recent development, elev8on Private will offer North American actors, creators, athletes and other high-profile individuals the chance to take stakes in assets financially, either alone or in a small group, or explore a brand partnership through an ‘influence for equity’ model. The latter will see the person exchange use of their name and image in exchange for a stake in a European company. The person will also agree to taking on a creative or commercial role at the company. Related Stories News French Microdrama App Shortstory Opens $1.1M Funding Round News Gérard Depardieu Drops Appeal Against Sexual Assault Verdict & Acknowledges Guilt In Statement Titled 'I Hear'.

Recent findings suggest that elev8on co-founder Florent Lamy gave Deadline the example of actor investing in a French brand and helping it launch across Europe. As part-owner, their own profile grows among European audiences. Watch on Deadline.

After identifying a potential fit, Elev8on will work with talent’s agents, managers and business managers “from the first conversation” and negotiate roles, commitments and participation. The initiative is to keep interest private with identities, figures and particulars held under confidentiality agreements.

Industry observers note that “Together with Anato, we’re already working on mandates across wine and spirits, sport, hospitality, lifestyle, beauty and tech,” he added. “We help each client choose the right company, negotiate their role and stake, and stay involved as the partnership develops. Anato handles due diligence and structures the deal.”.

Anato, which has offices in Paris and Bordeaux, will structure deals across French, Luxembourg or Swiss investment vehicles, and notes it will work alongside the investor’s own legal, tax and business advisors.

American entertainment industry figures and sport stars have become increasingly keen on European investments, with Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds notably becoming owners of Welsh soccer team Wrexham AFC, and helping it rise through the ranks of English football.

In a recent development, tom Brady was a part-owner of Birmingham City, but sold his shares and is now rumored to be eyeing a stake in Premier League team Chelsea. Michael B. Jordan owns a piece of Bournemouth AFC, and Snoop Dogg has stakes in Swedish fintech biz Klarna and Germany-based medical cannabis and health firm Sanity Group. Leonardo DiCaprio and Will.i.am. are other prominent Americans who’ve got investments in European businesses.

Elev8on represents the likes of Holt McCallany, Megan Fox, Djimon Hounsou, Haley Joel Osment, Keke Palmer, Elisha Cuthbert and Ben Feldman, and has a production arm that has been developing European superhero IP. It has offices in Paris, London and Los Angeles, with a focus on finding U.S. work for European talent and vice versa. Lamy, Elev8on’s CEO, founded the business with Daniel Blanc, who is the manufacturer’s President.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that olivia Rodrigo performed her somber yuletide ballad, “Miss This Christmas,” for the first time live at her concert in Nashville Monday night, Nov. 23.

“Miss This Christmas” was included on the B-side of the vinyl version of Rodrigo’s first holiday single, “Take Me Home (4 Christmas),”  which was released earlier this month. But the song still hasn’t gotten a wide digital release, and as Rodrigo noted in her introduction, “no one’s ever really heard it before.” (Though some unauthorized rips have popped up online.).

It has been revealed that the performance began with Rodrigo singing over a simple piano accompaniment, the arrangement later blooming with choral vocals and a tender guitar line. Lyrically, “Miss This Christmas” is the obverse of “Take Me Home (4 Christmas),” with Rodrigo tending a broken heart and passing along a message to an ex: “Next year’s gonna look real different/Tell your folks I’ll miss this Christmas.”.

Sources indicate that rodrigo spoke a little bit more about her two Christmas singles while introducing “Miss This Christmas.” She described “Take Me Home” as a “really fun song about my fantasy of having a boyfriend that takes me to his parents’ house for the holiday.” But, “in proper Pretty Sad for a Girl In Love fashion,” Rodrigo continued, “there’s a very happy A-side of the album and a very sad B-side. So it’s the same with the Christmas song.”  Trending Stories Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Snapshots From Miley’s Wedding: ‘Beautiful’ to See Family ‘United by Love’ Anthem Singer Apologizes for ‘O Canada’ Flub at Leafs-Islanders Game U2 Will Bring Their ‘Greatest Show on Earth’ Stadium Tour to North America in 2027 Watch Taylor Swift Surprise Brenda Lee With ‘Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree’ Honor.

Prior to her two-night stand at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena, Rodrigo stopped by Jack White’s Third Man Records to cut a live-to-acetate performance in the label’s famous Blue Room venue. The performance consisted of two 20-minute and included a fitting cover of the White Stripes classic, “Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground.”.

The current leg of Rodrigo’s Unraveled Tour in support of her Grammy-nominated album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl In Love, will continue through next month, wrapping Dec. 20 in Las Vegas. She’ll return to the stage in 2027 two lengthy residency in Los Angeles (Jan. 12 through 29) and Brooklyn (Feb. 11 through 28).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Industry observers note that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE.

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:.

He is among the upcoming breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

It has been revealed that chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the upcoming season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2.

Recent findings suggest that the final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

There will be five added minutes.

According to recent reports, chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

In a recent development, chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Gemini Notebook's Fresh Interactive Site Builder Is Much More Useful Than I Expected

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • In a recent development, that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • It has been revealed that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something new. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

In a recent development, that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

It has been revealed that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

To make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

In a recent development, with a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but claims you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Recent findings suggest that here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

It has been revealed that the finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a upcoming window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

In a recent development, I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

Everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

For something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

In a recent development, I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

Maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a massive family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a fresh website.

According to recent reports, bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

Netflix has revealed a trailer for its upcoming scripted series surrounding the infamous unsolved killing of JonBenét Ramsey.

Released Tuesday, the trailer opens on the early hours of December 25, 1996, when JonBenét’s parents John (Clive Owen) and Patsy (Melissa McCarthy) wake to find their daughter missing and a ransom note on their kitchen counter. A piano version of “Silent Night” sounds quite ominous as it lingers in the background of the trailer, which zeroes in on investigators’ suspicions regarding the child’s own family.

Sources indicate that “I was fascinated by the challenge of doing something that was a murder mystery without an ending, without being solved,” showrunner and executive producer Richard LaGravenese remarked in a statement. Related Stories Casting David Tennant Joins 'The Four Seasons' As Series Regular: "The Perfect Addition To Our Ensemble" News BBC To Launch CBeebies Hub On Netflix.

The trailer makes it clear that the slaying itself will just scratch the surface of the story that unfolds in the six-episode series. Watch on Deadline.

The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey, which will premiere just short of the 30th anniversary of the six-year-old beauty queen’s death, centers on one of the most infamous unsolved murder cases in American history, and the devastating personal and public reckoning that followed the death of JonBenét Ramsey on Christmas night in 1996.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to the trailer, which is embedded above, Netflix also released a few photos from the upcoming series. Find those below.

The Murder Of JonBenét Ramsey is co-written by Harrison Query and Tommy Wallach, directed by Anne Sewitsky and showrun by LaGravenese. LaGravenese, Query, Wallach, McCarthy and Sewitsky executive produce with Glasser, Ron Burkle, Bob Yari, David Hutkin for 101 Studios.

The cast includes McCarthy (Patsy Ramsey), Owen (John Ramsey), Emily Mitchell (JonBenét Ramsey), Garrett Hedlund (Det. Steve Thomas), Alison Pill (Det. Linda Arndt), Shea Whigham (Alex Hunter), Owen Teague (Shane Edwards), Clifton Collins Jr. (Det. Tom Trujillo), Angus Caldwell (Burke Ramsey), Jaime Ray Newman (Amelia Hunt), Rory Cochrane (John Eller), Chris Bauer (Chief Tom Koby), Will Patton (Lou Smit), Jeremy Bobb (Pete Hofstrom), John Billingsley (Santa Bill McReynolds), Josh Stamberg (Reed Hunt), Margo Martindale (Nedra Paugh), and Tzi Ma (Dr. Henry Lee).

All six episodes stream December 10 on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer. But if your lesbian-forward supernatural horror series isn't drawing cries of "blasphemy!"...what are you even doing? In that spirit, we'll conjure up some other shows dealing with the (extremely) dark side of high school.

Industry observers note that this time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate. There are ambiguous teases of the supernatural here (much more ambiguous than in The Body), but there's plenty of human-level horror as well. The show explores the nasty things we get up to when in survival mode (whether trapped in the wilds, stuck with other teenagers—or god forbid both at once), while also cynically (but accurately) positing that there's a huge difference between the version of the past we talk about and the one that really happened. Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

Situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It rapidly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

According to recent reports, juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

Recent findings suggest that mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that quickly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

Industry observers note that peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that the new Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

Four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

Upgrade, November 19, 4:46 p.m. ET: The release candidates are now available to public beta testers, with the same build numbers as the developer RCs.

In addition to macOS 27.3 beta 2, Apple is also rolling out the first Release Candidates for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4. Here are the details.

Two weeks ago, Apple released macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, along with macOS 27.2.1 Golden Gate, all of which included security fixes related to AirPlay, Bluetooth, and Messages, among others.

Today, the tech giant released the first RCs for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4, along with the second developer beta for macOS 27.3.

As is usually the case with direct-to-RC rollouts, Apple’s notes mention only that the updates provide ”security fixes for your Mac.” The actual release notes will likely become available soon after Apple officially releases macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4 in the coming weeks.

The build for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 RC 1 is 24H319, and the build for macOS Tahoe 26.7.4 RC 1 is 25G422.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to TVs, I'll be the first to admit I care more about aesthetics than performance. If I could hide mine entirely, I would. That's why Hisense's Canvas TV was so appealing when it first hit the market. A massive, blank screen had become an unwanted focal point in my otherwise thoughtfully decorated living room, and I wanted a better-looking alternative without paying a premium for Samsung's Frame TV.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve incorporated the Canvas TV into gallery walls in multiple apartments and now my own home with ease, surrounding it with matted photographs, framed artwork, and other decorative objects. And just in time for Black Friday, Best Buy has the Hisense 55-inch Hi-QLED CanvasTV on sale for $699. That's a massive 53% off with multiple screen sizes on sale.

In a recent development, the 2026 update of the Canvas TV pairs a crisp 4K picture with rich, vibrant Hi-QLED color and Dolby Vision support for enhanced contrast and detail. The 144Hz refresh rate helps reduce blur, whether you’re watching sports or playing video games. Plus, the new AI ambient light sensor automatically adjusts the screen’s brightness and color temperature to suit the lighting in your room, so you don’t have to waste time tweaking with the settings. It also runs on Google TV, giving you access your favorite apps without the need for an additional streaming device.

When we first reviewed the Canvas TV in 2024, we praised it as a value-friendly Samsung Frame TV dupe. It wasn’t without a few shortcomings, though. Our review found that the display could be quite dim, and that darker scenes often lacked detail and a cinematic feel. The original model was also limited to just two size options.

Sources indicate that hisense has made some worthwhile refinements over the years. While we haven’t officially reviewed the 2026 model, the improved Hi-Matte display is designed to do an even better job at minimizing glare and mimicking the appearance of art, while increased brightness should provide a more enjoyable viewing experience. The newer lineup also offers more sizes, ranging from 50 to 85 inches, along with additional frame finishes.

The latest version retains the very details that first made me a fan, however. I’m particularly fond of the included magnetic teak frame (no need to shell out for a separate decorative bezel!) and the ultra-slim wall mount that allows it to sit almost flush against the wall above my fireplace. That stated, I was equally happy letting it rest directly on my console in a former rental, where my landlord wouldn't allow TV mounts.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps my favorite upgrade? The art library has expanded from a few hundred to over 1,000 complimentary choices.

So if you, like me, would rather have art than a giant blank screen as your living room centerpiece, this is the Black Friday TV deal worth considering.

Industry observers note that amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Industry observers note that then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

In a recent development, if Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

According to recent reports, alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that newly introduced job listings on Apple’s website indicate the tech giant’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the firm has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple announced intends to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give consumers more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

According to recent reports, over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted new job listings that offer a closer look at its looks to develop autonomous AI agents:.

In one, Apple said it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

According to recent reports, today’s report on the latest job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring owners to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the manufacturer could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the new job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its prepares for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how promptly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally debuted its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

Over the last two years, AI greed has been largely to blame for rising prices across the tech world, from video game consoles to phones and laptops. It may have just claimed another victim, like Jason slowly tromping through Camp Crystal Lake.

A upcoming report from the Korean publication ETNews claims that Samsung will be shifting from an annual release of its Galaxy Watch lineup to a biennial cycle. By skipping 2027, the Galaxy Watch 10 would be the first one to not be released annually since Samsung debuted its first Galaxy smartwatch in 2018.

Sources indicate that now, as ETNews points out, "chipflation" is only partially to blame for this potential shift. However, it's certainly a major portion of it.

Samsung's Mobile eXperience (MX) division, responsible for the tech giant's smartphones, wearables, and more, has posted for profit losses for two quarters. The whole division is going through some major restructuring. That starts with Won-Joon Choi who was just unveiled as the new head of MX, less than four days ago.

Choi was previously the division's COO and led the introduces of the S26 and Galaxy Z Fold8 series.

Sources indicate that tom's Guide reached out to Samsung for confirmation but did not receive a response in time for publication. We will enhancement this article if the company responds.

The decision to delay the next Galaxy Watch is part of an aggressive push to make Samsung's mobile division more profitable. Part of that is streamlining the organization's product lineup.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Recent findings suggest that the increased prices of RAM and other key components have severely cut into Samsung's costs. Much of it is driven by Samsung's own chip fabrication division, which has fed into the AI chip frenzy.

Already, the company is reportedly cutting smartphone shipments by 30% with a focus on high-end models. A focus on premium, high-end models isn't new; other companies like Lenovo have already pursued it this year.

But also, the Galaxy Watch 9, a perfectly solid smartwatch, didn't move the needle when it debuted this summer. Plus, it suffered from a price hike as well. We praised the health insights that Samsung hasn't paywalled, unlike rivals, but at the end of the day its a more expensive Galaxy Watch 8. We didn't even include it in our picks for best smartwatch, a rarity for Samsung's usually excellent wearable.

“As hardware innovation has reached a mature stage, the company appears to have concluded that releasing latest products every year is no longer cost-effective," industry insiders told ETNews.

According to ETNews, the gap year could be filled in by fresh software updates and enhancements to existing health tracking features.

According to recent reports, also, Samsung may release its own Galaxy Fit model à la the recently released Google Fitbit Edge and Fitbit Air. Samsung has had versions, but nothing fresh has really hit in the last three years. Though at the beginning of November, a new fitness track was leaked as potential rival to the Fitbit Edge.

Sources indicate that perhaps, RAMageddon aside, this should be the model. In recent years, excitement for upcoming phones, watches, and other annual tech hasn't really hit because, like EA Sports' ongoing Madden franchise, these iterative updates typically don't really justify the cost of upgrading.

Besides, Samsung already does this with the "Classic" model and the newer Galaxy Watch Ultra high-end watch, both of which are on two year cycles.

A year or more of development time could finally bring about true innovation and change.

It has been revealed that after releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the manufacturer is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with latest privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several new features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

According to recent reports, and speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing owners to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful patch, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and users on the public beta can now try out these fresh features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

Did you spot anything upcoming in today’s beta? Let us know in the comments.

Sources indicate that if you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

If you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the tech giant is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

Industry observers note that the standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

Sources indicate that I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Sources indicate that amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Amazon Health: Prime owners get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance aims, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV reveals, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers new free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

#177124. Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2881 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer claims it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to significant problems.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • It has been revealed that andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer claims it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to significant problems.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

It has been revealed that andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he states he has identified the next significant shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Ng’s current efforts are focused on his tech giant Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he notes can yield “small data” solutions to significant complications in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

The great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

Andrew Ng: This is a significant question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

Sources indicate that ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a fresh paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

Ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

Having remarked that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of customers, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing manufacturer with millions of users.

Ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from major data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and stated, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Sources indicate that over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing new here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

Industry observers note that ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and remarked, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

In a recent development, the data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one organization or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that showed up.

It has been revealed that you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from major data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

Industry observers note that when you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand upcoming model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having remarked that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For big data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

For example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very quickly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

Recent findings suggest that could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. Upcoming tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an key piece of the puzzle.

According to recent reports, one of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

According to recent reports, ng: In AI, data cleaning is notable, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention quickly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

It has been revealed that for example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

Ng: I think synthetic data is an important tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

Industry observers note that “In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion people. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

According to recent reports, synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

To make these concerns more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a company approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

In a recent development, ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

One of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

How do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

Ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift matter. I find it really important to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and update the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

Industry observers note that in the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion customers. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Sources indicate that ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent latest neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s important for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

According to recent reports, ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to owners on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the patch becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

It has been revealed that this rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company declared four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.
