The inspiration for Apple’s newly introduced coming-of-age drama movie is so clear that even the title doesn’t try to hide it. But imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. I can’t say this Apple original looks like a critical darling-in-waiting, but hopefully it’ll offer some feel-good fun. And surely it can’t be received worse than the 2010 “Karate Kid” reboot, right?

Industry observers note that chris Pratt stars as Uncle Jake, a US Navy SEAL staying with his older sister, Sarah (Linda Cardellini), over the summer after being injured in the line of duty. Taking his nephew, Marc (Jude Hill), under his wing, Jake resolves to help him learn to stand up for himself against a pack of school-year bullies. Cue the epic training montage and scenes of family bonding.

Watch on Apple TV starting November 25.

I’ve got a personal reason to recommend “The Magic Faraway Tree.” The original Enid Blyton books were a childhood favorite, so seeing characters like Moonface (Nonso Anozie) and Saucepan Man (Dustin Demri-Burns) on the big screen transported me to a simpler time. The fantasy adventure is a whimsical ride, and clearly made with younger viewers in mind. Grown-ups might find it a little too simplistic, but if you’ve got young kids, I bet they’ll love it. Just don’t blame me if they want to watch it on repeat for weeks.

Recent findings suggest that starring Andrew Garfield, Claire Foy, Nicola Coughlan and Rebecca Ferguson (who’s deliciously wicked as the villain, Dame Snap), “The Magic Faraway Tree” sees a family move from the massive city to the countryside in hopes of a simpler, technology-free life. Once in their new digs, the family’s three children discover a magical tree full of quirky inhabitants, and if that wasn’t exciting enough, the tree can also transport them to dazzling fantasy lands.

Watch on HBO Max starting November 27.

Recent findings suggest that I can’t say that Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson would have been my first choice if you’d asked me to assemble a dream duo for a “buddy” action movie, but it’s a combination that works surprisingly well in practice. Which isn’t to say “Runner” is flawless; the plot is very pedestrian, but the action is entertaining, and Ritchson and Wilson’s dynamic is great.

According to recent reports, ritchson plays a former soldier, now working as a “runner,” essentially a courier for high-value items, both legal and illegal. Tasked with making a critical medical delivery, he reluctantly teams up with an unlikely ally, Wilson’s Ben Bishop. A young girl’s life hangs in the balance, and the job is complicated when the pair become the target of a criminal cartel. “Runner” is a fast-paced action-comedy, with a pair of likable leads. It’s disposable fun.

Watch on Hulu starting November 27.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1477 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially introduces the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 latest features—including one feature the tech giant trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger complications. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this newly introduced feature here.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.3 also comes with a fresh setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Currently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the major screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

It has been revealed that with watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

In a recent development, with iOS 27.3, however, the tech giant is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these upcoming Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company states Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

In a recent development, despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing newly introduced abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you strategy a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These upcoming actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Industry observers note that apple started testing its latest Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

In a recent development, apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

In a recent development, apple is also testing latest StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

Recent findings suggest that "Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with substantial iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

If you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the newly introduced updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

  • Free Joan Little has won numerous awards, including Best Documentary at the LA Shorts International Documentary Festival, and Best Short Documentary at the Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival in Arkansas, Morehouse College Human Rights Film Festival in Atlanta, the Teaneck International Film Festival in Fresh Jersey, and the Reel South Award from the RiverRun International Film Festival in North Carolina.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Sabrina S. Gordon and Oscar-nominated actress Danielle Brooks have joined the award-winning short documentary Free Joan Little as executive producers.

Sources indicate that the Oscar-contending film, directed by Yoruba Richen, “recounts the groundbreaking 1975 case of a young Black woman in eastern North Carolina who killed a white jailer after he attempted to rape her,” according to a synopsis. “Little’s flight from custody and the ensuing media frenzy galvanized a nationwide movement for her cause, with support from civil rights icons Angela Davis and Rosa Parks.”.

Free Joan Little has won numerous awards, including Best Documentary at the LA Shorts International Documentary Festival, and Best Short Documentary at the Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival in Arkansas, Morehouse College Human Rights Film Festival in Atlanta, the Teaneck International Film Festival in Fresh Jersey, and the Reel South Award from the RiverRun International Film Festival in North Carolina. In addition, the documentary has made the prestigious shortlists for the Cinema Eye Honors and the IDA Documentary Awards.

Watch the film’s trailer below.

It has been revealed that sabrina S. Gordon produced the Oscar-shortlisted Seeds (2025), Black Girls (2024), To the End (2024), and Flint (2020). In a statement, she said, “When Yoruba first showed me Free Joan Little as a work in progress while we were teaching a filmmaking workshop together in The Gambia, I knew immediately I wanted to support it however I could. Its artistic craft is as breathtaking as Joan’s remarkable story of defiance. Her courageous, uncompromising stand for bodily autonomy and human dignity against racism and sexual violence makes this film as urgent and relevant today as it was 50 years ago.”.

Danielle Brooks, who earned an Oscar nomination for 2024’s The Color Purple, serves as the voice of Joan Little in dramatizations within Free Joan Little.

“I am so moved by Joan’s story and am committed to making sure that her story is heard and seen by all,” commented Brooks. “I am proud to join the filmmaking team as an executive producer and to support the film in any way possible.”.

Sources indicate that “We were deeply honored when Danielle Brooks agreed to lend her voice to Free Joan Little, and welcoming her now as an Executive Producer—alongside Oscar-shortlisted filmmaker Sabrina Schmidt Gordon (Seeds)—is an extraordinary gift,” remarked Richen. “Sabrina is a longtime creative collaborator and dear friend whose vision as a producer, editor, and strategist has shaped so many acclaimed documentaries. Bringing Joan Little’s story back into the national consciousness is as urgent today as it was in 1975. Partnering with Danielle and Sabrina, along with Reel South, PBS North Carolina, and Black Public Media, allows us to ground this vital piece of Southern Black history in its local roots while delivering its powerful message of self-defense and justice to a nationwide audience.”.

Sources indicate that free Joan Little is directed by Yoruba Richen, featuring the voice of Danielle Brooks. It is produced by Christalyn Hampton and Bonnie Bertram for Promised Land Film, in association with Retro Report. Executive producers are Sabrina Schmidt Gordon (Vespertine Films), Danielle Brooks, and Kyra Darnton. Hannan Vanderlan edited the film; Keith Walker serves as director of photography. Reggie Dokes composed the score. The film also featured the 1975 song “Joan Little,” written by Bernice Johnson Reagon and performed by Sweet Honey in the Rock.

Sources indicate that the film makes its international premiere in London on Friday at the Women of the Lens Film Festival. It will be showcased in Cinema Eye Honors Short List screenings in Latest York and Los Angeles in December. Free Joan Little has been acquired by Reel South and PBS North Carolina for local-to-national public media distribution, including streaming on YouTube.

Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Michael Carrick remarked he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.
  • Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.
  • The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Carrick remarked he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

Post-match video footage indicated Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

According to recent reports, michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

In a recent development, “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”.

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

Industry observers note that “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”.

Industry observers note that all over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

It has been revealed that there have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Recent findings suggest that lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Industry observers note that both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

In a recent development, chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Recent findings suggest that tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

Recent findings suggest that PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off.

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

And it’s a debut for Tielemans.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Recent findings suggest that lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Recent findings suggest that slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Sources indicate that having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Sources indicate that amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

It has been revealed that united continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Recent findings suggest that worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

It has been revealed that heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

Sources indicate that united are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

Recent findings suggest that united seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Sources indicate that good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Recent findings suggest that bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their upcoming vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

A reminder of how they line up.

According to recent reports, man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee.

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier.

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”.

In a recent development, “They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”.

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Here’s a goal to dine out on...

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm.

Sources indicate that 📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm.

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊.

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how latest signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those upcoming signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

According to recent reports, “I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager stated. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

In a recent development, “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s tech giant. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”.

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

#177112. Breaking: I tested the iPhone 17, 17e, 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and Duo — here’s what I’d buy for Black Friday

Breaking: I tested the iPhone 17, 17e, 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and Duo — here’s what I’d buy for Black Friday

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the single biggest shopping day of the year is almost here, and you’ve probably seen many offers claiming to be some of the best iPhone Black Friday deals around.
  • It has been revealed that the beauty of Apple’s current lineup is that it’s the most diverse it’s ever been, covering different form factors and budgets — so I’m pitting the iPhone 17, 17e, Air, 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and Duo against each other.
  • Having tested all of them, I’ll break down which iPhones are actually worth your money this Black Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the single biggest shopping day of the year is almost here, and you’ve probably seen many offers claiming to be some of the best iPhone Black Friday deals around. But before you make an impulsive decision, it’s worth knowing which of the current models is actually worth your money.

It has been revealed that the beauty of Apple’s current lineup is that it’s the most diverse it’s ever been, covering different form factors and budgets — so I’m pitting the iPhone 17, 17e, Air, 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and Duo against each other. With Black Friday deals rolling out across major carriers and retailers, it’s pretty tricky determining which one of them is the right fit.

Having tested all of them, I’ll break down which iPhones are actually worth your money this Black Friday.

6.1-inch Super Retina XDR display (2,532 x 1,170).

6.3-inch Super Retina XDR (2,622 x 1,206).

6.5-inch Super Retina XDR (2,736 x 1,260).

6.3-inch Super Retina XDR display (2,622 x 1,206).

6.9-inch Super Retina XDR display (2,868 x 1,320).

7.6-inch Super Retina XDR (1,878 x 2,670).

5.4-inch Super Retina XDR (1,398 x 2,034).

18MP Center Stage camera (f/1.9).

18MP Center Stage camera (f/1.9).

Black, Silver, Glacier, Burgundy.

Black, Silver, Glacier, Burgundy.

Frankly, the iPhone 17e is the one I’d recommend buying the least. What makes it an even tougher sell is that it launched at $599 earlier this year, but has since been given a $100 price hike that brings it to $699. Despite that, the iPhone 17e remains the most affordable entry point into Apple’s current lineup if you’re buying unlocked without any carrier deals or bundles attached.

It covers the basics of what I’d want in a modern iPhone, like 256GB of starting storage, all-day battery life, speedy A19 performance, and a pocket-friendly build. Even though it runs iOS 27 just like all the others, it doesn’t make the cut for Siri AI — which is a bummer if you want a smarter, more proactive assistant. At the same time, it’s the only iPhone in the stable that is still stuck with a 60Hz refresh rate.

In terms of utility, you’re only getting a single 48MP main camera on the back — though I can’t overlook the fact that it performs well above average, including in low light. In fact, I was surprised in my iPhone 17e vs Pixel 10a face-off how its single rear camera held up.

But as I said at the beginning, I can’t recommend getting this one knowing that the next model in the lineup exists.

In a recent development, if there’s one model in the lineup that hits the sweet spot for almost everyone, it’s the iPhone 17 — and yes, it too got a $100 price hike a couple of months back that now puts it at $899. Even with that increase, it’s easy for me to recommend for a number of reasons.

For that small jump over the iPhone 17e, you get a vastly smoother 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display, faster 35W wired and 25W MagSafe charging, and way better color options to choose from. Sure, it’s running the same A19 chip as the iPhone 17e, but its faster 120Hz refresh rate makes a huge difference in making UI animations look and feel smoother.

It has been revealed that more importantly, the iPhone 17 delivers a far more satisfying camera experience. Pairing its 48MP main sensor with a dedicated 48MP ultrawide lens, this setup gives me more creative flexibility with my shots. I’ve broken down everything about them in my iPhone 17 vs. iPhone 17e face-off, which resulted in a lopsided win for the iPhone 17.

When it launched, I had so much excitement and buzz for the iPhone Air — until I actually started using it. As impressive as its 5.6mm titanium frame feels in the hand, the iPhone Air is another model that’s tough for me to recommend — especially now that Apple’s $100 price hike pushes its starting cost to a steep $1,099.

You’re paying a serious premium strictly for thinness, while getting less functionality compared to the rest of the group. It doesn’t help either that the iPhone 17 sits below it at $200 less.

In a recent development, the biggest trade-offs show up in daily use. Even though you get a gorgeous 6.5-inch 120Hz OLED display and speedy A19 Pro performance, its battery capacity is dramatically limited by its razor-thin profile — resulting in noticeably shorter battery life and slower charging than the rest of the lineup. Worse yet, it’s also stuck with just a single 48MP rear camera like the iPhone 17e. You don’t get an ultrawide lens, no macro shots, or definitely no telephoto zoom on a phone that costs $1,000-plus. We've even put its camera to the test against the iPhone 17e and I was shocked by how the iPhone Air barely came out on top.

Don’t get me wrong, I miss the days of thin and light phones, but when I’ve gotten accustomed to modern phones that pack dual cameras and easily get me through an 8-hour work shift without worrying about running out of juice, it’s so hard to go back to anything less.

Without question, I’d recommend looking out for Black Friday deals on the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max. If you want the best of what Apple makes, both the $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro and $1,299 iPhone 18 Pro Max earn an easy recommendation from me. Yes, Apple hit both models with a $100 price hike this year and added a bit of heft — but they justify their premiums.

For starters, they’re packing a blazing-fast A20 Pro chip under the hood, offering access to the full Siri AI suite, and sporting a triple-48MP camera system headlined by a versatile new variable-aperture main lens.

No matter which one you end up getting, I love the fact that Apple still gave both phones identical camera hardware, 60W wired charging, and Pro Controls that make them more of a photographer’s camera. While the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max inherently has the bigger screen and battery, I personally find the smaller iPhone 18 Pro much easier to handle. Ultimately, choosing between them comes down purely to size preference.

Sources indicate that either way, you won’t question the decision to buy either one. And quite frankly, they’re well worth the cost over the iPhone Air.

Apple’s first foldable is easily the most exciting iPhone in years, and despite its steep $1,999 starting price, I still recommend buying it if you want a compact phone that unfolds into a mini tablet. Its sturdy titanium frame, nearly invisible crease, and nano-texture inner display, make it feel far more refined than a typical first-generation device.

In a recent development, having a pocketable 5.4-inch outer screen is great for when I want to use it one-handed, and I also love how it opens into a 7.6-inch canvas unfolded with intuitive split-screen multitasking in iOS 27. Not only does its unique design make it perfect for creators who want to shoot videos of themselves by pairing the outer screen with the superior rear cameras, but it’s also an absolute powerhouse for everyday productivity — something none of the others can match to the same degree.

In a recent development, of course, you still have to accept a few trade-offs compared to the $1,299 iPhone 18 Pro Max. You’re giving up Face ID, a dedicated telephoto zoom lens, no variable aperture, and no Pro Controls, while some third-party apps still aren’t fully optimized for the wider inner display.

Even with those compromises, nothing else in Apple’s lineup matches the Duo’s versatility — and if you can soften the blow with a Black Friday trade-in deal, I don’t think you’ll regret the purchase.

Delta-E color accuracy (lower is better).

When it comes to outdoor visibility, the iPhone Duo takes the crown with a blinding peak brightness of 2,558 nits. It’s an intriguing find because of its nano-texture display. While it’s still viewable outdoors, it lacks the contrast and vibrant color tones of the Pro models — with the iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone 18 Pro topping out at an impressive 2,326 nits and 2,314 nits, respectively.

According to recent reports, stepping down to the middle of the pack, the iPhone Air reached 1,678 nits, while the standard iPhone 17 hit 1,505 nits. I think both are plenty bright for everyday outdoor use. Unsurprisingly, the iPhone 17e trails the entire group at 1,002 nits.

Geekbench 6 (single-core/multi-core).

3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited (score/fps).

In a recent development, our benchmark testing draws a clear line between Apple’s A19-powered models and the newer A20 Pro flagships. The iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo all run on the A20 Pro chip — and, as a result, deliver class-leading CPU speeds, with Geekbench 6 scores clustering tightly around 4,700 single-core and 12,700 multi-core.

On the graphics front, the iPhone 18 Pro edges out the pack in 3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited with a score of 38,667, just ahead of the 18 Pro Max at 38,474 and the Duo at 36,515.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the A19-equipped iPhone 17e and iPhone 17 trail noticeably behind in both CPU and GPU performance, while the A19 Pro inside the iPhone Air offers only a slight uptick over the standard 17. Even so, all three handle everyday apps effortlessly.

Average Battery life (Hrs:Mins).

If battery endurance is notable to you, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max truly separate themselves from the rest of the pack. In our battery test, the iPhone 18 Pro Max led the way with an average of 18 hours and 27 minutes, while the smaller iPhone 18 Pro wasn’t far behind at 16 hours and 17 minutes.

Meanwhile, the rest of the lineup clusters tightly around the 12.5- to 13.5-hour mark. The iPhone Duo edges out the non-Pro models at an average of 13 hours and 20 minutes, while the iPhone 17 and iPhone Air came in at over 12 hours.

At the end of the day, I recommend looking out for Black Friday deals on the iPhone 17, iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and the iPhone Duo. While the iPhone 17 is a great entry point for everyday customers and the iPhone Duo delivers unmatched foldable versatility, the iPhone 18 Pro takes the crown as the best overall balance and value of the bunch.

You get the exact same blazing-fast A20 Pro performance, variable-aperture triple-camera system, and speedy 60W charging as the pricier iPhone 18 Pro Max — all in a much easier-to-handle size that saves you $100 upfront. Unless you specifically crave a massive screen or a folding display, the iPhone 18 Pro is the one I’d look out for Black Friday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios has inked an overall deal with Ullisses Campbell, the award-winning Brazilian journalist and crime writer, as it digs deeper into the true crime genre in Brazil.
  • Industry observers note that campbell is well-known in Brazil, and is one of the writers on Amazon MGM Studios’ prison drama Tremembé, which has been a hit for Prime Video in Brazil.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios has inked an overall deal with Ullisses Campbell, the award-winning Brazilian journalist and crime writer, as it digs deeper into the true crime genre in Brazil.

Industry observers note that campbell is well-known in Brazil, and is one of the writers on Amazon MGM Studios’ prison drama Tremembé, which has been a hit for Prime Video in Brazil. Now the studio has locked Campbell into a deal that will see him work across its whole true crime slate as well as on latest projects.

“Our country is home to extraordinary stories, many of which are stranger than fiction,” stated Campbell. “Brazil’s history is also told through its crimes. Many of these cases reflect the customs, prejudices, inequalities and social shifts of their time. When screen adaptations revisit these events, they also create a historical record and help preserve our collective memory. That is why I see true crime as a lens to understand who we are and how we got here.” Related Stories News Everything We Know About Amazon MGM & Sony Pictures TV's 'God Of War' Adaptation So Far Casting 'Upgraded 2' Film Casts Tanner Zagarino, Christopher McDonald, Andrea Arcangeli & Alessandro Preziosi.

Recent findings suggest that campbell wrote a series of books about Tremembé, a real-life prison that has housed some of Brazil’s most notorious criminals. Inmates have included Suzane von Richthofen, Elize Matsunaga and the Cravinhos brothers. The drama series Tremembé, which Campbell co-wrote with Vera Egito, Juliana Rosenthal, Thays Berbe and Maria Isabel Iorio, is heading into Season 2. Watch on Deadline.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a franchise, definitely,” Julia Priolli, Head of Creative for Brazilian Originals at Amazon MGM Studios, told Deadline about expanding the Tremembé IP. She added there will be some infamous fresh inmates in the upcoming run of the show. “For Season 2, we’re bringing five new characters, including Robinho, the football player [imprisoned after being convicted of rape].”.

Campbell will exec produce Season 2 of Tremembé, which launches in 2027. Speaking more broadly about the Amazon MGM deal with the journalist, writer and producer, Priolli mentioned he will have input into the true crime docs, series and films the studio is working on.

In a recent development, “It could be as an exec producer, or sometimes it will be doing research, because he’s very strong when you need to go deep into aspects of a story and he really has great access,” she mentioned. “It doesn’t matter if we’re talking about a documentary, or if it’s a movie or a scripted series, we want his input across everything. We’re talking to him about some fresh indicates that we haven’t announced yet, but basically, we want him across the whole true crime slate.”.

Priolli explained that Amazon has linked up its production, streaming and publishing businesses in Brazil as it pushes deeper into ripped from the headlines crime content.

Recent findings suggest that “We tried to identify, here in Brazil, what would be the best true crime stories for us and we wanted to use the whole flywheel that we have at Amazon for telling these stories. We not only have the studios where we could do a movie or a documentary or a scripted series, but we also have Audible, where we can do those as audio, we have Kindle, we have Amazon Books.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 is at the moment in beta testing with developers and public beta owners. The enhancement includes multiple newly introduced features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 ….

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone customers sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final upgrade.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 people, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a upcoming Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

In a recent development, reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 also brings a upcoming face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a newly introduced option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with upcoming clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

It has been revealed that this includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The upgrade also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the revision expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so consumers can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

It has been revealed that there are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

Recent findings suggest that with iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple claims it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

It has been revealed that you can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 is a major enhancement to Safari. First, the update adds support for a latest vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music owners, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

Industry observers note that there are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the enhancement introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Recent findings suggest that second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a upcoming “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Here are a few other changes in iOS 27.3:.

EXCLUSIVE: Jon Kilik (The Hunger Games, Foxcatcher, Babel) has joined Jana Hojdová’s documentary Oscar contender Robert Richardson: The White Devil as an executive producer.

The intimate portrait of three-time Academy Award-winning cinematographer Robert Richardson, who collaborated with Oliver Stone, Quentin Tarantino and Martin Scorsese on many films, explores the artist behind some of the most iconic images in modern cinema.

Producer Kilik and Richardson share a connection dating back to their time at the University of Vermont, where both studied under influential film professor Frank Manchel in the 1970s. Related Stories Festivals Robert Richardson Interview: The Three-Time Oscar Winner On Working With Oliver Stone, Predicting Tarantino's Next Move, And The Wildest Shoot He Ever Worked On - Karlovy Vary News B-Rated Acquires Robert Richardson Documentary Featuring Quentin Tarantino & Martin Scorsese Ahead Of Karlovy Vary -- First Look Trailer.

Sources indicate that their careers have also intersected through their separate collaborations with filmmaker Stone: Kilik produced Stone’s Alexander, while Richardson served as cinematographer on numerous Stone films, including Platoon, JFK, Born on the Fourth of July, Nixon. Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, kilik’s other credits include Spike Lee’s Do the Right Thing, Malcolm X, 25th Hour, Da 5 Bloods; Julian Schnabel’s The Diving Bell and the Butterfly and At Eternity’s Gate; Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Babel and Biutiful; and Bennett Miller’s Foxcatcher. He also produced the first four films in The Hunger Games franchise.

According to recent reports, “It’s an honor to be part of Jana’s beautiful film that skillfully blends a lifetime of Bob’s personal archives with a front row look behind the scenes of some of the greatest films and greatest directors of the last 40 years. As Quentin T states in the film, ‘There is Robert Richardson and there is everyone else,’” noted Kilik.

Robert Richardson: The White Devil traces the unlikely creative partnership between Hojdová and the cinematographer, when she was a cinematography student at Prague’s FAMU film academy, and reached out to him for a university project.

It has been revealed that what began as a student thesis evolved into a years-long collaboration and personal friendship. Richardson granted Hojdová access to hundreds of hours of private video archives and welcomed her into his personal and professional world, resulting in an unusually candid portrait of the cinematographer.

Industry observers note that “I’m truly honored that Jon Kilik is joining our project. His work on films I deeply admire has been a great source of inspiration to me, and I feel incredibly grateful and excited to have him on board,” remarked Hojdová.

Featuring Richardson alongside filmmakers Stone, Scorsese and Tarantino, as well as Kate Hudson and Woody Harrelson, the documentary explores Richardson’s creative vision, uncompromising artistic temperament and extraordinary career.

It has been revealed that richardson is one of the most celebrated cinematographers in film history, having received three Academy Awards on JFK, The Aviator, Hugo and seven Academy nominations. His collaborations with Stone, Scorsese and Tarantino have helped shape the visual language of contemporary American cinema.

It has been revealed that the film premiered at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival and had its U.S. premiere at DOC NYC in New York this month. It is represented by sales tech giant B-Rated International and seeking US distribution.

Sources indicate that advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling new approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.
  • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.
  • That goal also was supposed to set up penalties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ latest set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

Sources indicate that after a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

In a recent development, while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Recent findings suggest that had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Recent findings suggest that johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

Industry observers note that that was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Industry observers note that johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

It has been revealed that as if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The upcoming season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Industry observers note that chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our proposal and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, steven Hack, an original member of Broadway‘s Cats and A Chorus Line who went on to gain numerous credits on stage as well as in such TV series and films as Thor: The Dark World, American Horror Story: 1984, Criminal Minds, Scrubs, Fresh Off The Boat, General Hospital and many more, died November 19 at his home in Los Angeles following a sudden and unexpected cardiac event. He was 68.

His death was confirmed by Los Angeles’ Interact Theatre Tech giant, of which Hack was a founding member.

Born on April 20, 1958, in St. Louis, Hack eventually studied at the California Institute of the Arts (CalArts) and the American Academy of Dramatic Arts (A.A.D.A.), making his professional debut as a teenage dancers in the 1978 film Grease, just before making his Off Broadway debut in the musical Coolest Cat in Town.

In 1982 Hack joined the original production of the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical Cats as an understudy, over five years with the show playing the roles Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Coricopat and others. From there he took the role of Greg in the national tour of A Chorus Line, and was with the organization when it returned to Broadway for its celebratory and record-breaking 3,389th Broadway performance on September 29, 1983. Watch on Deadline.

Stack performed in numerous other stage productions outside of Broadway, including Off and Off Off Broadway productions of Counsellor-at-Law with John Rubinstein, which also ran for seven months in Los Angeles. A founding member in 1989 of Los Angeles’ acclaimed Interact Theatre Tech giant, Stack performed in many of the company’s productions including Death of a Salesman, Our Town, The Laramie Project, A Little Night Music; he was nominated for Ovation and A.D.A. awards for his one-man play Willie’s Son.

A member of the Television Academy for more than 20 years, Hack’s many TV credits include of Perry Mason, Pam & Tommy, American Horror Story 1984, Ratched, Marvel’s Agent Carter, Criminal Minds, The Newsroom, The Mentalist, Bones, Weeds, The New Adventures of Old Christine, Desperate Housewives, Days of Our Lives, Scrubs, The West Wing, Everybody Loves Raymond, General Hospital, Seinfeld, Mad About You, and many others.

Film credits include, among others, Minority Report, Fantastic Four, Thor: The Dark World, The Happytime Murders, and Intolerable Cruelty.

In announcing his death, Interact Theatre Firm artistic director Barry Heins and executive director Walter Ware III wrote, “As we remember Steven, we celebrate not only his many contributions to our company, but also the joy of knowing and working with him. He will always hold a special place in Interact’s history and in the hearts of those who knew him.

“We extend our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, and all who loved him,” they continued.

Complete information on survivors was not immediately available.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

Sources indicate that the club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

Sources indicate that ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

In a recent development, 'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but swiftly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

In a recent development, salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

It has been revealed that they are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ says Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

Sources indicate that like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

Sources indicate that 'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady mentioned that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

Recent findings suggest that intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

Sources indicate that city have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

Industry observers note that he utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

The format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

According to recent reports, ‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson states, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

#177098. Industry News: 'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (825 w)
